leads.title: Qanun Jinayat (2014 Aceh Sharia Criminal Code)
leads.documents: Aceh legal status: criminalizes consensual adult same-sex sexual acts, punishable by up to 100 lashes or up to 100 months (8 years) imprisonment. Core Aceh risk law for trans-visitor dossier.
leads.detail: Cited in text as 'Under the 2014 Qanun Jinayat, consensual same-sex sexual acts between adults are punishable by up to 100 lashes or up to 100 months (8 years) imprisonment.' No URL visible in provided text.

leads.title: 2005 Aceh Sharia Authorization / Aceh anti-homosexuality law
leads.documents: Aceh enforcement machinery: 2005 grant of right to introduce Sharia Law for Muslim residents; Aceh enactment punishing gay sex with 100 lashes, set for enforcement by end of 2015.
leads.detail: Cited as 'In 2005, the Indonesian government gave Aceh Province the right to introduce Sharia Law... punish anyone caught having gay sex with 100 lashes. The law was set for enforcement by the end of 2015.' No URL visible.

leads.title: 2017 Aceh public caning case - two young gay men aged 20 and 23
leads.documents: Documented enforcement incident in Aceh: two men sentenced to being caned in front of public for same-sex conduct.
leads.detail: Cited as 'In 2017, two young gay men (aged 20 and 23) were sentenced to being caned in front of the public in the Aceh province.' No URL visible.

leads.title: January 2018 North Aceh police operation against twelve transgender women
leads.documents: Targeted anti-trans enforcement in Aceh: arrest of 12 transgender women, forcible hair-cutting, compelled men's clothing, closure of beauty salons.
leads.detail: Cited as 'In January 2018, police in North Aceh arrested twelve transgender women, forcibly cut their hair, compelled them to wear men's clothing, and closed their beauty salons.' No URL visible.

leads.title: January 2018 Aceh parlour raid / torture and public parading
leads.documents: Documented incident of torture/humiliation of LGBTQ/trans persons in Aceh: ransacked parlour, shaved heads of transgender women, stripped shirts and bras, paraded forcing them to shout 'to become men'; criticized by human rights organisation.
leads.detail: Cited as 'In January 2018, the Aceh police ransacked a parlour with support from the Aceh autonomous government... shaved the heads of transgender women, stripped their shirts and bras, and paraded them in the street while forcing them to shout "to become men".' and 'transgender women were arrested, stripped naked, had their heads shaved, and were publicly shamed in the province of Aceh.' No URL visible.

leads.title: 11 August 2025 Aceh public caning sentence for kissing
leads.documents: Recent Aceh enforcement: two men aged 20 and 21 sentenced to public caning for kissing after April arrest when police broke into toilet.
leads.detail: Cited as 'On 11 August 2025, two men, aged 20 and 21, were sentenced to public caning for kissing. They were arrested in April after police broke into the toilet.' No URL visible.

leads.title: Indonesian Ulema Council (MUI) Fatwa - March 2015
leads.documents: Religious-legal pressure: declares homosexuality curable disease, calls for same-sex acts to be punished by caning and in some instances death penalty; cited as moral guidance not positive law.
leads.detail: Cited as 'In March 2015, Indonesian Ulema Council (Majelis Ulama Indonesia or MUI) issued a fatwa... called for same-sex acts to be punished by caning, and in some instances, the death penalty.' Plus DPR response that fatwa only serves as moral guidance. No URL visible.

leads.title: Constitutional Court of Indonesia Decision - 14 December 2017 (5-4)
leads.documents: National court ruling on criminalization attempt: rejected Family Love Alliance petition to erase 'underage' in Article 292 and amend Articles 248, 285, 292 to criminalize gay sex and sex outside marriage; held issue for legislature.
leads.detail: Cited as 'On 14 December 2017, the Constitutional Court... issued a 5-4 ruling rejecting a petition... sought to erase the term "underage" in article 292, in order to persecute all same-sex sexual conducts.' No URL visible.

leads.title: Vivian Rubiyanti Iskandar case - legal gender recognition precedent
leads.documents: Trans rights machinery: first trans Indonesian legally recognized as female; establishes court-approved legal gender change after sex reassignment surgery and judge approval, enabling opposite-legal-gender marriage.
leads.detail: Cited as 'cases like Vivian Rubiyanti Iskandar (the first trans Indonesian to be legally recognized as female) giving rise to legal recognition of trans Indonesians' actual genders by the State' and 'allowed to change their legal gender on official documents after undergoing sex reassignment surgery and after receiving a judge's approval.' No URL visible.

leads.title: National Police Chief Regulation No. 8 of 2009 and 2015 hate-speech circular; Human Rights Law No. 39/1999
leads.documents: Rights-protection machinery: police duty to protect special rights of minority groups including sexual orientation; 2015 circular to process hate speech related to sexual orientation and gender identity; constitutional/human-rights law theoretical employment discrimination protection.
leads.detail: Cited as 'Regulation of the Head of the National Police... Number 8 of 2009 stipulates the duty of the police to protect the special rights of minority groups, including in the terms of sexual orientation' and 'police authorities ruled a circular letter since 2015 that it would process any hate speech related to sexual orientations and gender identity' and 'Human Rights Law (No. 39/1999).' No URL visible.
